headline: THE bone age number
subhead: IS MEASURED FROM THE WRONG BONES

headline: Disclaimer:
body: For educational purposes only. This is a walkthrough of two published studies, not medical advice and not a call to action.

headline: #1 Where Does Bone Age Come From
body: Bone age is read from an X-ray of your hand and wrist. One image, one number, then that number gets used to estimate how much growth your entire skeleton has left. | Which only works if the hand and the legs are on the same clock. They are not, and the gap is massive.
punch: Your hand is not where your height comes from.

headline: #2 The Hand Finishes First
body: Dolan et al in PLOS Biology checked when different bones in the same animal fuse. In mice, *epiphyseal fusion*, the growth plate disappearing for good, hit the phalanges at **3 weeks** and metacarpals at **4 weeks**. The tibia and femur? Still open at **12 weeks**. | Rats, same order: **12 weeks** phalanges, **16 weeks** metacarpals, legs still open.
punch: _Small bones close while the long bones are barely started._

headline: #3 They Also Run Slower
body: At one week the metacarpal was growing at **49%** of the tibial rate and *proliferation per column*, basically how many times the cells in one stack divide, was **46%**. | Every marker of *growth plate senescence*, which is the plate slowly running out of divisions like a battery draining, was further along in the hand bones at every age.
punch: ==Your hand bones grow at half speed and drain faster.==

headline: #4 Why: IGF Signalling
body: They took *chondrocytes*, the cells that build the plate, out of finger bones and leg bones. Finger cells divided slower. Then they added IGF-1 to the finger cells and proliferation rose **to match the untreated leg cells**. | So the cells are basically identical. The finger bones just get less growth signal, kinda like the same engine with less fuel line.
punch: The bone is the same. The signal is not.

headline: #5 The Human Data
body: MRI of the wrist, knee and ankle in **958 people** aged 14 to 21. Fusion timing varied by site inside the same person and complete fusion happened about **2 years earlier** in girls. | *Pubertal stage* correlated with fusion at every site, **0.514 to 0.598** in males. Your birthday did not get tested against it, but puberty stage clearly tracks.

headline: #6 What Actually Tracked Maturation
body: **BMI correlated** with growth plate maturity, 0.186 to 0.384. **Physical activity** had no significant correlation in males at any site, and in females one very low correlation at the wrist, **0.095**, nothing else. | What separates this from the usual advice is that it was tested directly in 958 people, and training basically did not register.
punch: ==Being heavier tracked faster maturation. Training did not.==

headline: TL;DR
subhead: HOW TO READ YOUR OWN X-RAY
body: Bone age = estimate from your fastest ageing bones, not your legs. Track pubertal stage, that is the variable that correlated. And the hand finishes first, always.
